title: Coefficient transport of section invariants and normalized deformation comparisons
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $n\geq1$, put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, and let $R\to B$ be a unital map to a finite commutative ring. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-coefficient pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their bounded intrinsically constructible finite-Tor subcategories [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], and the constructible adjoints $Rg_{!,D}\dashv g_D^!$ for $D=R,B$ [sk-prop-sf-existence, sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. For $D=R,B$, write $D_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ for the constant ring sheaf on the small etale site, and define $D_T(1)=\nu_T^*(\mu_{\ell^n,T}\otimes_{R_{T,\mathrm{et}}}D_{T,\mathrm{et}})$, where $\nu_T$ is the small pro-etale to etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $\mu_{\ell^n,T}$ is the etale sheaf $U\mapsto\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^{\ell^n}=1\}$, with $R$ acting by powers, as in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; put $D_T(0)=D_T$ and $D_T(r)=D_T(1)^{\otimes_D r}$ for $r>0$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These are the locally free rank-one Tate lines and canonical pullback identifications of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Fix the coefficient-independent compactifications of these morphisms in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $(-)_B$ for [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] and $c_g:(g_R^!R_S)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}g_B^!B_S$ for the counit-characterized comparison of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional].

For a smooth separated map [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] $g:V\to S$ of pure relative dimension $r\geq0$ with a closed section $s:S\to V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], $g\circ s=1_S$, put $C_D(g,s)=Ls^*g_D^!D_S$. Let $D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_S$ be the geometric deformation space $\operatorname{Bl}_{s(S)\times\{0\}}(V\times_S\mathbf A^1_S)\setminus\widetilde{V\times\{0\}}$ (the tilde denotes strict transform), with its induced smooth map $\widetilde g$ and section $\widetilde s$. Here [def-pur-dnc-section-family] specifies the coefficient-independent geometric deformation space, its structural map and its section; let $\pi_N:N_s\to S$ be the actual normal-bundle projection with zero section $0_N:S\to N_s$ [def-pur-normal-bundle]. Put $F_D=L\widetilde s^*\widetilde g_D^!D_{\mathbf A^1_S}$ for each $D=R,B$. At $D=R$ this is the family object of [def-pur-dnc-section-family] at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and level $n$; the displayed formula defines the corresponding object at the arbitrary finite ring $B$. Use affine space [def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $a:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ and $i_j:S\to\mathbf A^1_S$ ($j=0,1$) be the projection and its two sections. Identify the fibres with $C_D(g,s)$ and $C_D(\pi_N,0_N)$ using the canonical smooth base-change exchanges (mates of compact-support base change). Define
$$q_{g,s}:(C_R(g,s))_B\xrightarrow{\sim}C_B(g,s),\qquad q_F:(F_R)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}F_B$$
by the canonical pullback/tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] followed by $Ls^*c_g$, respectively $L\widetilde s^*c_{\widetilde g}$.

For any smooth separated $k$-morphism $g_0:V_0\to S_0$ of pure relative dimension $r_0\geq0$ between schemes in the same setting, with no section assumed, let $h:S'_0\to S_0$ be any $k$-morphism from a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Put $V'_0=V_0\times_{S_0}S'_0$, and write $g'_0:V'_0\to S'_0$ and $h_V:V'_0\to V_0$ for the projections. Write $c_{g_0}$ and $c_{g'_0}$ for the same counit-characterized comparisons defined above. The canonical smooth base-change exchanges $e_D:h_V^*g_{0,D}^!D_{S_0}\to(g'_0)_D^!D_{S'_0}$ are isomorphisms. The coefficient comparisons commute with this exchange, namely, under the canonical pullback/tensor identifications,
$$e_B\circ h_V^*c_{g_0}=c_{g'_0}\circ(e_R)_B.$$ In particular $q_{g,s}$ and $q_F$ respect the two displayed fibre identifications and the corresponding comparisons for the normal-bundle pair. They also respect etale localization of pairs. On a standard coordinate pair $(\mathbf A^r_S\to S,0)$ they are the canonical identification $(R_S(r)[2r])_B\simeq B_S(r)[2r]$.

Let $\kappa_R:F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C_R(g,s)$ be the normalized family comparison of [prop-pur-dnc-family-constancy], applied at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and level $n$. Under pullback/tensor identifications, the map
$$\kappa_B=a^*q_{g,s}\circ(\kappa_R)_B\circ q_F^{-1}:F_B\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*C_B(g,s)$$
is the unique isomorphism whose restriction at $i_1$ is the identity under the canonical fibre identification. On each etale coordinate chart carrying the pair near its section to the standard pair, this isomorphism is the constant-family identification normalized to the identity at $t=1$; these restrictions specify the direct coordinate comparison over $B$. Consequently, writing $\delta_D:C_D(g,s)\to C_D(\pi_N,0_N)$ for the inverse of $i_0^*\kappa_D$, one has
$$\delta_B\circ q_{g,s}=q_{\pi_N,0_N}\circ(\delta_R)_B.$$
These assertions include relative dimension zero and the zero coefficient ring.
